extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors, journal editors, and peer reviewers of in vivo animal experiments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing manuscripts that report experiments using live animals, specifying the minimum information and recommended contextual items needed for transparency, reproducibility, ethical assessment, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the 'Essential 10' — a basic minimum that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research. Essential for readers/reviewers to assess reliability of findings. (No detailed sub-guidance on this page excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Essential 10' minimum reporting requirements. Reviewers should expect clear reporting of how sample sizes were chosen and any calculations or justifications used to determine them. (No item-specific details provided in this excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'Essential 10' item — manuscripts must report criteria for including or excluding animals or data so readers can judge potential bias and validity. (Further examples not present in the excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 'Essential 10' as a required element. Authors should report whether and how animals/units were allocated randomly to experimental groups to reduce allocation bias. Reviewers should check for this information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'Essential 10' reporting item — manuscripts should state whether and how blinding (masking) was used during allocation, conduct, and outcome assessment to reduce detection/performance bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Essential 10' — authors should clearly define primary and secondary outcome measures so readers can interpret results and assess whether analyses match pre-specified outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'Essential 10' requirement: report the statistical approaches used to analyze data, including tests, models, assumptions checked, and software, so results can be evaluated and reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals (species, strain, sex, age)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential reporting item requiring clear description of animals used (at minimum species, strain, sex, age) so findings can be interpreted and compared across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 'Essential 10' — authors must describe procedures in sufficient detail to allow replication (what was done, how, when, and why).

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the 'Essential 10' elements — manuscripts must report results transparently (including measures of precision and variability) to allow assessment of effect sizes and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Recommended Set' that complements the Essential 10 by providing contextual summary information for readers; recommended to include concise, informative abstracts that reflect methods and key findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended contextual item — authors should provide scientific background and rationale to place the study in context and explain why the research question is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Recommended Set — manuscripts should state the specific objectives, hypotheses, or aims of the study to clarify the intended tests and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting item — include a statement of ethical approval, licensing, or justification for animal use and any steps taken to minimize harm, providing transparency for ethical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — report environmental and husbandry conditions (e.g., housing, bedding, diet, light cycles) that could affect animal physiology and experimental outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended item — describe care procedures, monitoring during experiments, humane endpoints, and any interventions to reduce suffering, which affect welfare and data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended: authors should discuss the meaning of the results, limitations, and their implications for the field, including how findings relate to existing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/translation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting: comment on the extent to which findings are generalisable beyond the specific experimental conditions and the potential for translation to other species/systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — where applicable, report whether the study protocol was registered or pre-specified, supporting transparency and reducing selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended: provide information on availability of study data and materials to enable verification, re-analysis, and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reporting item — disclose conflicts of interest, funding sources, and roles to allow readers to assess potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ARRIVE checklist by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer Use: Reviewers should use the ARRIVE checklist to ensure animal research papers report all essential information for reproducibility and ethical evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides peer reviewers to verify the presence of the 'Essential 10' items and consider the Recommended Set to ensure manuscripts provide sufficient information for reliability, reproducibility, and ethical assessment.
